evals.prompt: Use cuvslam-onboard to explain which PyCuVSLAM wheel fits an x86_64 Ubuntu 24.04 machine with Python 3.12 and an installed CUDA 13 toolkit. Give installation and verification commands only; do not install anything.
evals.expected_output: Select an x86_64 cu13 cp312-abi3 wheel from the official cuVSLAM release matching the desired version. Explain that CUDA is installed separately, show pip installation in a virtual environment, and verify import plus cuvslam.get_version().
assertions: Match architecture, Python ABI, and installed CUDA major when selecting the wheel.
Give install and import verification commands without executing installation or a source build.

evals.prompt: I am setting up cuVSLAM with one aligned RGB-D camera plus an IMU. Which mode supports this sensor combination, what build support is needed, and what camera-model limitation should I check? Explain only.
evals.expected_output: Use Multisensor, with a cuNLS-enabled build and pinhole cameras. One RGB-D camera supplies the required scale constraint, and an IMU is optional in this mode. Multisensor is experimental. Inertial requires stereo plus IMU and is not the mode for this rig.
assertions: Choose Multisensor for RGB-D plus IMU.
Explain the cuNLS, pinhole-camera, and experimental-status constraints.

evals.prompt: I already have cuVSLAM checked out at /workspace/cuVSLAM, a Release build at /workspace/cuvslam-build, and a Python environment at /workspace/cuvslam-env. Give the commands to install PyCuVSLAM from that build and explain what to do after rebuilding the C++ library. Do not execute them.
evals.expected_output: Reuse the supplied checkout, build, and environment. Set CUVSLAM_BUILD_DIR=/workspace/cuvslam-build for pip install /workspace/cuVSLAM/python/. Reinstall the Python bindings after each C++ rebuild because of the scikit-build-core limitation.
assertions: Use the supplied paths without asking for clone or environment destinations.
Set CUVSLAM_BUILD_DIR and explain the required reinstall after rebuilding.

evals.prompt: Help me configure a new offline PyCuVSLAM mapping example. Which Tracker mode and odometry/SLAM synchronization settings must agree, and what does later map localization need? I only need an explanation.
evals.expected_output: Use Tracker.Mode.OdometryWithSlamOffline, Odometry.Config(async_sba=False), and Slam.Config(sync_mode=True). The tracker rejects mismatched mode/configuration. Save the map after mapping and supply an initial pose hint and images for localization.
assertions: Specify all three matching offline settings.
State that localization needs an initial pose hint.

evals.prompt: My cuVSLAM environment is ready. Export a TUM trajectory.txt from my recorded KITTI sequence; this is a pose-file task, not installation.
evals.expected_output: Do not activate cuvslam-onboard. Route to cuvslam-trajectory if available, and resolve the dataset location before replay. Do not start an onboarding or live-camera workflow.
assertions: Recognize recorded pose export as a trajectory task.

evals.prompt: My existing Isaac ROS visual_slam installation runs, but stereo tracking jumps during turns. Help diagnose the failure rather than setting up a new installation.
evals.expected_output: Do not activate cuvslam-onboard. Route to cuvslam-troubleshoot if available and begin diagnosis of the existing tracking problem.
assertions: Do not clone or reinstall cuVSLAM as the first diagnostic action.
